Drawdown: two rules computed; headline = max drawdown in 2021Q1–2024Q4. The first rule (peak = max in 2021–2023 window) hid drawdowns for markets that recovered to new highs inside the window (AU); the switch is a window-artifact fix made before correlations were interpreted, both variants stored
Test 2 sample rule: numeric floating-rate stock shares only (IMF Table A5 + RBA + HKMA); JP variant excluded because BOJ never tightened in 2022–23, so the treatment was not applied

test1_money_vs_price.verdict: FAIL/WEAK: money variables alone do not rank 2010–2024 nominal house-price growth across the 12 markets (rho ≈ 0.15–0.22). Largest wrong-way points: MY (highest real rate, near-top price growth), KR (high M2, near-bottom growth), HK (lowest real rate, mid growth). Supports the framework only in its full form: money without the institutional/supply terms has no cross-sectional ranking power.

spearman_excl_JP.reason: BOJ did not tighten; natural experiment condition absent

test2_downside_stickiness.verdict: SUPPORTED (moderate): among markets that actually tightened, higher floating-rate share ranks with deeper 2021–24 nominal drawdowns (rho −0.68, n=7). MY annotation: predominantly floating yet max drawdown −0.2% — the institutional-stickiness residual (HDA, developer holding) the framework predicts.

test5_state_classification.question: Can the pre-declared state rules (SPEC N) classify markets as primed/capped IN ADVANCE, with primed delivering systematically better forward 3-5y returns?

rules_as_applied.S1: volume/inventory series at <=30th percentile of own trailing 10y (midrank percentile); fixed series per market: US = months supply of new houses (FRED MSACSR), UK = HMLR sales volume, TW = MOI transfer registrations; others N/A
rules_as_applied.S2: mortgage rate at <=20th percentile of own trailing 10y; series: US MORTGAGE30US, AU RBA F5 FILRHLBVS, CA BoC V80691335 5y conventional, UK BoE IUMTLMV SVR, TW CBC 5-bank new housing loan rate, MY BNM ALR (2008+); NZ/JP N/A. The yield-carry alternative was used nowhere (no verified historical yield series)
rules_as_applied.S3_C2: BIS total credit to households %GDP via FRED Q**HAM770A, Q4 values; S3 = fall >=3pp vs T-5; C2 = level >=80 or rise >=5pp vs T-5; TW N/A (not a BIS reporter)
rules_as_applied.S4_C3: price-to-income = OECD HPI_YDH annual mean (US/UK/AU/NZ/CA/JP), TW = MOI 房價所得比; S4 = below own trailing-15y median; C3 = >=15% above it; MY N/A
rules_as_applied.C1: inventory >=70th pct of trailing 10y — only the US has an inventory-type series (MSACSR); all others N/A
rules_as_applied.classification: primed: S>=3 & C<=1; capped: C>=2 & S<=1; else neutral. N/A scores 0 and is counted; markets with fewer than 3 computable S-rules can never reach primed (TW has 3, MY/NZ/JP have 2) — disclosed, not patched
rules_as_applied.forward_returns: BIS nominal index annual averages (TW: Sinyi Q4), T to T+3 / T+5, judgment years 2000-2021

calibration_checks.US_2019: NOT primed (S=1/4: rates not bottom-quintile, volumes not compressed, PTI at median; only S3 hit). The rules missed the 2019-2021 US boom. Reported as-is.
calibration_checks.TW_2019: NOT primed (S=1/3: volumes had already recovered by 2019 so S1=0, PTI above 15y median so S4=0; S2 hit). TW 2016-2018 came closest at S=2/3 with S3 unavailable (TW not a BIS credit reporter). Reported as-is.
calibration_checks.MY_2016_2020: Never formally capped: only C2 computable for MY (C max 1 < threshold 2). C2 fired 2014-2016 and 2020; forward 3y returns then fell to 4.6-9.0% for T=2017-2020 judgments, directionally consistent with the site thesis, but the strict rules cannot issue the capped label. Insufficient data, disclosed.
calibration_checks.JP_all_years: Never primed (S1/S2 unavailable caps S at 2 - a data limitation, disclosed) and never capped (deleveraging kept C2=0; post-crash PTI kept C3=0). The deflation-era declines (2000-2008, f3 -2 to -17%) therefore sit in the NEUTRAL bucket: the rules did not catch Japan falling, and could not have caught Japan rising. Falsification verdict: no false signal issued on Japan, but no skill demonstrated either.

honest_verdict.as_upside_finder: WEAK. Only 5 primed cases in 176 market-years, all US 2011-2016. Median 3y forward: primed 17.9% vs neutral 17.4% - no separation. 35 neutral cases delivered 3y >= 30% that the rules did not catch (early-2000s Anglosphere, post-COVID US/NZ/TW).
honest_verdict.as_false_positive_filter: STRONG in-sample. Zero primed cases below +10% at 3y; primed IQR tight (17.7-22.3) and all positive at both horizons.
honest_verdict.as_downside_classifier: PARTIAL. The only market-years with all three C-rules firing (US 2005-2007, C=3/3) preceded the only systemic crash in sample (f3 -15 to -27%). But 33 of 49 capped cases still returned >= +10% over 3y: the C2 debt-level trigger (>=80% GDP) marks AU/NZ/CA as capped for decades while they compounded. As written, capped means better-avoided tails (q1 +2.4% vs neutral q1 +7.7%), not falling prices.
honest_verdict.overall: The state machine, applied with pre-declared thresholds and no tuning, is an honest but narrow tool: it reliably avoids bad primed calls and it flagged the one true bust, but it finds few opportunities and mislabels chronically-leveraged compounders as capped. The thresholds were NOT adjusted after seeing these results, per the iron rules.

regime_conditioning.regime_rule: G3 central bank total assets (Fed WALCL, ECB ECBASSETSW, BOJ JPNASSETS via FRED; PBoC/BoE not available on FRED - G3 used, disclosed), year-end 12-month change converted to USD at annual-average FX (FRED DEXUSEU/DEXJPUS), divided by combined US+euro-area+Japan nominal GDP (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD). Thresholds fixed before computing: >+5% = easing, <-2% = tightening, else normal. Coverage 2003-2024 (WALCL starts Dec 2002; 2000-2002 N/A).
honest_notes: The rule was expected to also catch 2009 and 2012-13. It does not: 2009 prints -0.95% (Fed assets roughly flat year-end-to-year-end after the late-2008 spike, which the rule dates as easing-2008), and 2012-13 print +0.7%/+1.7% (ECB balance-sheet contraction offset Fed QE3). Reported as-is; thresholds not adjusted.
USD conversion embeds FX valuation effects: yen depreciation deepens the measured 2022 tightening.
regime_conditioning.strata_note: all_normal = forward 3y window entirely in normal years; crosses_regime = window overlaps at least one easing or tightening year; windows touching 2000-2002 (regime unknown) excluded. Every judgment year 2017-2021 has its forward window inside the 2020-2024 regime storm.
regime_conditioning.reading: Primed-vs-neutral separation is clearer in all-normal windows (22.3 vs 16.6 median). The capped bucket is harmless in normal windows (median 20.6) and does its damage where windows cross regimes (q1 -1.2): busts in this sample happen around regime shifts, not in calm conditions.
regime_conditioning.us2019_reframed: Under the regime frame, the correct statement of the US-2019 miss is: the framework should not be asked to predict a global liquidity flood, but it should be able to rank who rises most when the flood arrives.

easing_window_cross_section.dependent: nominal HPI change 2019Q4 to 2021Q4, BIS quarterly (TW: Sinyi Q4), 12 markets

cohort_25_39_momentum_2015_2020.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024, PopulationByAge5Group medium/estimates CSV, ages 25-39 both sexes

easing_window_cross_section.reading: Same flood, different boats: the 2020-21 rise ranks best on young-cohort momentum (rho +0.44; NZ top on both, JP/HK/TH bottom), ahead of money growth (+0.29) and the real rate (-0.12, right sign, negligible). Taiwan is the clear wrong-way point (cohort shrinking, prices +22%), suggesting a money-substitute demand channel the slow variables do not carry. First calibration of the v2 slow layer: moderate, not strong.
